mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue to drive retail and recreation activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility, as observed in the most recent week, signals a stronger return to office-based work, which will directly boost weekday retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days following a week where WORKPLACES rose by more than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent upward trend in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting and daily routines, which will collectively increase foot traffic to retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing continued upward trends.

mechanism_narrative: In a 'reopening' regime, if RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated above baseline, it indicates a continued preference for staying home, which will act as a persistent drag on the full recovery of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly increases, even while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 10% of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The recent strong increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, indicating more frequent essential outings, will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation as people combine errands, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases or remains flat, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility, as seen in the most recent data, suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure, which will redirect some recreational spending and activity towards indoor retail and recreation venues over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains unchanged in the week following a week where PARKS mobility fell by more than 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high while WORKPLACES mobility also increases, it indicates a prevalent hybrid work model, which limits the full recovery of RETAIL_REC due to fewer daily commutes and more localized, less diverse spending patterns over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly increases, despite both RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES remaining elevated above their baselines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS mobility over the next two weeks, following recent fluctuations, indicates a seasonal shift away from outdoor activities, which will naturally redirect leisure and recreation spending towards indoor retail and recreation venues.
candidate_trigger: PARKS shows a sustained decline over two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat over the next 14 days, despite PARKS mobility showing a sustained decline.
